canonical_topic: Off-Peak to Peak Price Ratio as a Storage Valuation Input
definition: A rule-of-thumb relationship between overnight (off-peak) and peak power prices that can be used to estimate storage value, noting that this ratio is seasonal rather than fixed.
core_idea: In many regions overnight power is roughly half the price of peak power on a typical basis, but the ratio shifts by month — summer afternoons see peak prices spike from air-conditioning demand while nighttime prices stay comparatively stable, narrowing the share of energy used at night.
key_points: Overnight power described as 'about 50 percent' the price of peak power in many regions — presented as an illustrative typical figure, not a universal constant.
The ratio varies by month (illustrated in the source's Figure 4.8.5).
Summer peak prices spike due to air-conditioning demand on hot days; nighttime prices remain relatively stable.
This relationship could underlie a model that estimates peak prices from marginal fuel costs and then derives off-peak price estimates from those.
trading_implications: Storage valuation models using this ratio should account for month-to-month variation rather than applying one fixed ratio year-round.
caveats: Treating the ~50% off-peak/peak ratio as a fixed constant rather than a seasonally varying approximation.
